items.name: Your Profile
items.tagline: Design and build a personal profile page in Figma and HTML/CSS
items.build: A personal profile page — designed in Figma, built in HTML and CSS, live on the web
parts: Figma designs for desktop and mobile
HTML and CSS build from scratch — no frameworks
Responsive layout that works on any screen
A deliberate typography and colour system
Deployed to a public URL
items.constraint: No default fonts. No templates. Typography and colour must be a conscious decision you can explain.

items.name: The Brief
items.tagline: Build a responsive site for a real client brief
items.build: A responsive website built to a real brief from a real person outside the course
parts: Client kickoff meeting and written brief
Wireframes and prototype in Figma
HTML and CSS build with real content
Responsive across mobile and desktop
Delivered and handed over to the client
items.constraint: The client is real. The content is theirs. You are solving their problem, not making a portfolio piece.

items.name: Game On
items.tagline: Build a working browser game from scratch
items.build: A working browser game built entirely in vanilla JavaScript
parts: Game loop and state machine
DOM manipulation for rendering
Collision detection or equivalent game logic
Score system and player feedback
Start screen and game-over state
items.constraint: A stranger must be able to pick it up and play it without any instructions from you.

items.name: Level Up
items.tagline: Add UI, interaction and sound to your game
items.build: Your Sprint 3 game — refactored, extended with UI, audio, and persistent scores
parts: Refactored codebase — no spaghetti code
Start menu and settings screen
Sound effects and music via the Web Audio API
High scores saved with localStorage
Visual polish — transitions and feedback animation
items.constraint: Sprint 3 code must be refactored, not just extended. You must be able to explain every line.

items.name: Live Data
items.tagline: Build a web app that reads and writes to a real database
items.build: A web application that reads and writes to a live database
parts: SQL database with at least two related tables
Full CRUD — create, read, update, delete
Web interface with forms and validation
Server-side logic handling the data
Deployed and accessible by URL
items.constraint: Real data. Real operations. A stranger must be able to use it without guidance.

items.name: Ship It
items.tagline: Integrated Project — a full digital product combining all Year 1 skills
items.build: An integrated digital product combining design, code and data — demonstrated live in a crit
parts: Product brief and concept statement
Design in Figma and build in HTML, CSS, JavaScript
Working database integration
Deployed live and accessible by URL
5-minute crit presentation to an external reviewer
items.constraint: You present to someone outside the class. Not a link submission — a live demonstration in front of people.

items.name: Fix It
items.tagline: UX-research an existing product and design a better version
items.build: A redesign of an existing digital product, backed by UX research and user testing
parts: Heuristic evaluation of the original product
3+ user interviews with documented findings
Affinity diagram and key insights
Figma prototype of the redesign
Usability test of the prototype with real users
items.constraint: Every design decision must trace back to a finding. Opinion without evidence is not accepted.

items.name: Test Your Assumptions
items.tagline: Prototype and test with real users — then do it again
items.build: A prototype designed, tested with users, and then significantly changed based on what you learned
parts: Low-fidelity prototype (paper or Figma)
User test session — recorded or documented
Analysis of what failed and why
Revised prototype with changes clearly documented
Before/after comparison with justification
items.constraint: Something must change as a result of testing. 'It tested fine' is not a finding.

items.name: Code as Medium
items.tagline: A creative coding experiment — generative, interactive or data-driven
items.build: A creative coding piece — generative, interactive, or data-driven — where the code is the design
parts: Concept statement — what it does and why
p5.js, Canvas API, or equivalent
Responds to input — mouse, keyboard, touch, or live data
Live demo or recorded performance
Short written reflection on intention and outcome
items.constraint: Not a website about something. A thing in itself. It must do something when you interact with it.

items.name: Real App
items.tagline: An advanced web application pulling from a live API
items.build: A web application that integrates a real external API and handles live data gracefully
parts: API integration with authentication where required
Async JavaScript — fetch, promises, or async/await
UI designed around the shape of the data
Error handling for API failures and empty states
Deployed and accessible
items.constraint: Must handle real-world conditions: slow connections, empty results, API errors. All of these must fail gracefully.

items.name: Pick a Stack
items.tagline: Build a site or app with a modern framework of your choice
items.build: A site or app built with a modern JavaScript framework — chosen and justified by you
parts: Written framework choice with justification
Component-based architecture
State management
Build pipeline and deployment
README with setup instructions for another developer
items.constraint: You chose the framework. You own the decision. You must be able to explain why it was right for this project.

items.name: The Full Build
items.tagline: Software Project — a complex system built end-to-end with a team
items.build: A complex full-stack system designed and built by a team, from architecture to deployment
parts: Architecture diagram agreed by the team before a line is written
Git workflow — branches, pull requests, code review
Front end, back end, and database all connected
Technical documentation
Team retrospective and individual contribution log
items.constraint: Real team. Real roles. Real codebase. Every team member must have commits in the repository.

items.name: Data Made Visible
items.tagline: A complex, interactive data visualisation with a real dataset
items.build: A complex interactive data visualisation built from a real dataset of at least 1,000 rows
parts: Dataset sourced, cleaned, and documented
D3.js, Observable, or equivalent
At least two linked views or interaction types
Annotations and text that explain what the data shows
Written methodology: what the story is and how you chose to tell it
items.constraint: The data must be real. The story must be verifiable. Every design decision must be documented.

items.name: Touch the Physical
items.tagline: A project using sensors, hardware and real-world interaction
items.build: A project where software and hardware meet — sensors, microcontrollers, and a real interaction
parts: Arduino or Raspberry Pi circuit with sensors or actuators
Data pipeline from hardware to web interface
Physical enclosure or installation
User testing in the physical space
Circuit diagram and code documentation
items.constraint: A real person must be able to use it without you explaining it to them.

items.name: Make Space
items.tagline: An immersive or spatial experience — XR, installation or generative
items.build: An immersive or spatial experience — XR, 3D environment, or physical installation
parts: Three.js, WebXR, or a physical installation
Spatial layout and navigation design
At least one interactive element
User journey mapped and tested
Exhibition setup and documentation
items.constraint: It must be experienced in space, not just viewed on a screen.

items.name: The System
items.tagline: A production-quality component library or design system
items.build: A production-quality design system with components, tokens, and complete documentation
parts: Design tokens — colour, typography, spacing
20+ components with documented variants
Accessibility audit — WCAG AA minimum
Live component documentation (Storybook or equivalent)
Getting-started guide for another developer
items.constraint: Another developer must be able to integrate it into a new project without asking you a single question.

items.name: Full Stack
items.tagline: A full-stack application with real architecture decisions
items.build: A full-stack application built with deliberate architecture decisions and documented reasoning
parts: Architecture Decision Record (ADR) document written before building
REST or GraphQL API with OpenAPI spec
Database schema with migrations
Front end consuming your own API
Deployment with dev and production environments separated
items.constraint: Every major technical decision must be documented. The architecture must be something you can stand in front of and defend.

items.name: Go Mobile
items.tagline: A mobile application with real users
items.build: A mobile application tested with at least 5 real users who have it installed on their phone
parts: React Native or equivalent cross-platform build
At least one native feature — camera, notifications, or location
App Store or Play Store draft listing with screenshots
5 real user test sessions with documented findings
Iteration on the app based on feedback
items.constraint: Five real users must have it installed on their phone. Screenshots of this are part of the submission.

items.name: Own the API
items.tagline: A back-end system with API design, security and scalability
items.build: A back-end system with authentication, rate limiting, and documentation built for third-party use
parts: OpenAPI specification written before the code
JWT or OAuth2 authentication
Role-based authorisation
Rate limiting and structured error responses
Integration test suite
Postman collection or equivalent for testing
items.constraint: A developer who has never spoken to you must be able to integrate your API using only the documentation.

items.name: Ship to Production
items.tagline: A DevOps pipeline — CI/CD, deployment, monitoring
items.build: A complete CI/CD pipeline — automated testing, deployment, monitoring, and incident response
parts: GitHub Actions or equivalent CI/CD workflows
Automated test suite — unit and integration
Docker containerisation
Cloud deployment with secrets managed securely
Monitoring dashboard and alerting
Runbook: what to do when it breaks at 2am
items.constraint: Merging to main must trigger an automatic deployment. Nothing is manual.

years.subtitle: Streams converge on the Major Project.

items.name: Define the Problem
items.tagline: Research phase — problem definition, literature review, methodology
items.build: A research proposal that precisely defines the problem you will spend Year 4 solving
parts: Literature review — minimum 10 sources
Problem statement of no more than 200 words
Methodology choice with written justification
Ethics review or statement
Project plan with milestones through to Sprint 20
items.constraint: 'AI and creativity' is not a problem. 'How generative image tools change the client brief process in small agencies' is. The problem must be specific enough to solve in two semesters.

items.name: First Version
items.tagline: A working prototype tested with real users or stakeholders
items.build: A working prototype — not a Figma mockup — tested with real people outside the course
parts: Functional prototype in code
3+ user test sessions with people outside IADT
Analysis report: what worked, what failed, what changes
Version 2 plan based on findings
Progress presentation to supervisor
items.constraint: Must be tested with people who are not on this course and do not know you personally.

items.name: Better
items.tagline: A refined, production-quality version based on honest critique
items.build: A refined, production-quality version of your project — improved in ways you can prove
parts: Documented changes from Sprint 18 with justification
Performance and accessibility improvements with evidence
Updated technical documentation
Final presentation drafted and rehearsed
Exhibition installation tested and ready
items.constraint: Every change must trace back to a Sprint 18 finding or a measurable improvement. 'I just thought it would be better' is not evidence.

items.name: On Show
items.tagline: Final submission, public exhibition and crit — the sprint model's endpoint
items.build: The finished project — submitted, exhibited publicly, and defended in front of an external panel
parts: Final code and documentation submitted
Public exhibition — physical installation or live demo at On Show
5-minute crit presentation to an external panel
Written reflection: what you made, why, and what you would do differently
Sprint portfolio: four years of documented work as evidence of development
items.constraint: Anyone walking in off the street should be able to understand what you made and why you made it.
